mem.10:
- **Mar 27, 2023:** Andrew had started a Financial Analyst job the previous week. Audrey had three dogs—Pepper, Precious, Panda—and had owned them for three years; she bought new collars/tags. They explored parks and trails. Andrew had no pets, loved animals (especially eagles, which he spotted hiking), and praised Fox Hollow as a weekend trail with great views.
- **Apr 2:** Audrey adopted Pixie, a small white puppy, bringing her total to four. Pixie needed days to adjust; she and Pepper initially needed time but now get along and often stay together. Puppy care postponed a hike. Andrew was considering a dog but struggled to find dog-friendly city housing; Audrey suggested pet-filter websites. They shared dog photos. Andrew missed hiking with his family dog and valued the bonds and memories hiking creates; Audrey liked the idea of hiking with her dogs.
- Andrew finds nature restorative, peaceful, and connecting—“at home in his soul”—especially amid life’s chaos. City life makes outdoor time difficult, so he tries to hike outside the city weekly for greenery, mountains, and fresh air. He photographs special moments to share nature’s peace.
- **Apr 8–9:** Andrew and his girlfriend tried a new city café, enjoying discovering places to eat and unwind; they had croissants, muffins, and tarts. Andrew shared a pastry-and-coffee photo.
- Audrey finds dog walks centering and recharging; her dogs mean the world to her. **Week of Apr 9–15:** she baked blueberry muffins (shared photo) and proposed a pastry party with Andrew; he agreed. Dogs invited, but no date/place set.
- **By Apr 16:** Audrey had an arm tattoo of a dog and sunflowers, symbolizing her bond with her dogs and love of nature; she wanted their happy faces with her when away. On Apr 16 she shared photos of dogs running and a woman walking dogs in woods.
- **Week of Apr 24–30:** Audrey saw a hummingbird darting with wings spread during a hike. **May 3:** Andrew found a nearby open space for hiking and found it refreshing.
- Audrey keeps her dogs safe on hikes with leashes and shoes. They love scents/nature, fetch (ball/frisbee), park playdates, toys and meeting dogs; tolerate party hats for treats. She recommended a nearby dog park with trees/benches; Andrew planned to visit. **May 5 (Friday):** she and the dogs road-tripped to a national park; she takes such trips about every couple months.
- **May 6:** Andrew was searching for a dog via websites, shelters, and friends; apartment life made him think a small dog would suit him. He considered space and breed exercise needs and sought pet-friendly housing near parks/woods. Audrey recommended a park near her home for walking her pup. He hadn’t found a dog and planned another shelter visit. May 6–7 weekend he hiked with friends and girlfriend at a newly discovered peaceful spot.
- **May 11:** Audrey said caring for four dogs takes much of her free time. She signed up for a June positive-reinforcement pet-bonding workshop after seeing a pet-store flyer and meeting a friendly, playful dog. She expected her quick-learning dogs to respond to rewards, opposed punishment, and planned to share tips/progress. Andrew said he’d look into classes. He shared a dirt path to a grassy hill; Audrey shared a group-dog photo with one dog circled in yellow; he called it adorable.
- **Jun 1:** Audrey took pups to a park to run/play off leash; their happiness gave her joy and peace. **Jun 2:** Andrew praised her and asked about her hiking trip, sharing a sunset mountain photo with a grazing horse. Audrey described a hike with dogs to a beautiful national-park peak the previous week (**May 22–28**): sunset, running dogs, breeze, birdsong; felt like paradise. She shared a favorite photo of two horses in a fenced field. Nature cheers her and makes her grateful. She asked about Andrew’s dog search.
- **Jun 2:** Andrew still couldn’t find a dog-friendly city home; discouraged but determined. Audrey offered to help and asked him to email housing criteria; he thanked her and they agreed to keep searching.
- **Jun 11:** Andrew and friends took a rock-climbing class. Beginner-challenging but satisfying; he reached the top, felt proud, and friends cheered. **Jun 13:** he shared a top-of-climb view and a man climbing. Inspired to try weekly outdoor activities like kayaking, maybe bungee jumping; nature helps him leave his comfort zone.
- **Jun 13:** Audrey invited Andrew for a walk with her dogs at a small park with a tree-surrounded trail she’d found the previous week; he accepted, but no time/date set. Dogs love meeting people. She shared photos of dogs playing ball/frisbee in a meadow. Walks usually last an hour with varied routes and exploring; dogs return tired and happy. Outdoors with them is her happy place. Andrew said nature calms, refreshes, and gives perspective; Audrey said it makes people feel alive and centered.
- **Jun 23:** Andrew hiked with friends; good weather, bird songs, tree smells, photos (not yet reviewed). **Jun 26:** Audrey had moved to a new place with a bigger backyard, shared two dogs on its lawn; dogs loved running, exploring, sniffing. She set up agility equipment/toys. Andrew shared a photo of dogs playing at a nearby indoor doggy daycare; Audrey planned to check it out. Andrew offered to find more dog-friendly places. They agreed pets are family and bring joy; Audrey couldn’t understand people hating/hurting them. Andrew also shared a colorful neighborhood-park flower bed. Audrey was unpacking. She shared photos of someone’s feet on a rock above a lake and someone sitting on a rock overlooking it, recalling a hike years earlier with friends at a stunning mountain lake. Andrew admired it; Audrey encouraged appreciating small things and taking nothing for granted.
- **Jul 3:** Audrey was taking a challenging but rewarding dog-training course; dogs already improving. She and Andrew had little time for new trails; Andrew still couldn’t find dog-friendly rental housing and was sticking to urban adventures. Audrey shared a photo of two dogs running with a ball. Her four dogs are all 3 years old: two Jack Russell mixes and two Chihuahua mixes, all mutts; they love running and fetch and form a great pack. She shared photos of two curled in a dog bed and two on a couch under a blanket. They’d had a fun, slightly crazy doggy playdate the previous Friday (**Jun 30**). Andrew was getting into cooking while unable to hike. Audrey loves cooking and offered family recipes. Her chicken pot pie recipe reminds her of her grandmother’s kitchen and conversations at the table; she shared pie photos and promised to send the recipe. Cooking is an escape, de-stressing and creative for both. Audrey likes music, a glass of wine, and going with the flow while cooking; she called it therapeutic/self-care. Garlic is her go-to ingredient. She offered a roasted chicken recipe: Mediterranean-inspired, with chicken, garlic, lemon, and herbs; easy, healthy, and her favorite comfort meal. Andrew thanked her, planned to try it, and promised to report back.
mem.19:
Andrew began a Financial Analyst job the week of March 20, 2023. He loves animals, especially birds and eagles, and spots birds while hiking. He recommends Fox Hollow for views. Nature makes him feel connected, restored, peaceful, and at home; city life makes access difficult. He tries to hike on weekends, enjoys greenery, mountains, and fresh air, and takes photos to share nature’s calming effects.

Audrey has four dogs: Pepper, Pixie, Precious, and Panda. By July 3, 2023, she described them as two Jack Russell mixes and two Chihuahua mixes, all three years old. Their personalities differ: the oldest is relaxed, the second playful, the third sometimes naughty but cuddly, and the youngest lively and adventurous. She calls them her most important companions and says they bring her joy, peace, meaning, love, and happiness. They like fetch, frisbees, trails, new scents, playdates, and exploring; Audrey uses leashes and shoes for safety. She walks them about an hour at their pace and says walks are their favorite part of the day. She also plays fetch, arranges dog-park playdates, and puts party hats on them for treats. Her nearby dog park has trees and benches. By June 26 she had moved to a home with a larger backyard and agility equipment/play area. Their favorite resting spots: Pepper—the couch; Pixie—the bed; Precious—the chair; Panda—the rug; they also cuddle together. By September 24 she said her dogs mostly play with one another, not other furry pals.

Audrey uses positive-reinforcement training and opposes punishment. She enrolled in a workshop for June 2023 and later took a challenging training course; by August 4 she was attending agility classes twice a week. She teaches obedience and tricks such as sit, stay, shake, and roll over, and says training is fun and rewarding. She recommends patience, regular training, time, love, and praise to build trust. She learned grooming in a course and recommends gentle, patient grooming, especially around ears and paws, plus daily brushing, baths, and nail trims. On August 16 she took all four dogs to the vet; it was chaotic, so she planned to take them one at a time. She might like more dogs someday, but four keep her busy. She makes personalized wooden name tags for pets. Her tattoos include a dog and sunflowers (love of dogs/nature), and later all four dogs. Her childhood dog Max loved fetch; she remembers long neighborhood walks and confiding in him. She sometimes road-trips with her dogs (about every couple of months); on May 5, 2023, they visited a national park. She once hiked to a peak there for sunset, breeze, and birds (May 26–June 1). She enjoys nature as refuge and restoration, likes lakes, and recalled a peaceful mountain-lake visit with friends. She has never fished.

Andrew initially considered adopting a dog but struggled to find dog-friendly housing. He searched websites and shelters, asked friends, contacted landlords, and wanted a home near parks/woods; he thought a small dog best for apartment living. Audrey offered to help find housing if he emailed his criteria. Andrew brought home Toby on July 11, 2023; by August 4 he described Toby as a young male German Shepherd, smart and loyal. Andrew wanted to bond with him and hike when feasible; Audrey advised that puppy care takes time, attention, walks, and activity. Andrew hoped to learn care himself and have outdoor adventures with Toby. In September, he still had not found dog-friendly housing, and Toby was too young for hikes.

Andrew and Audrey planned a hike with Audrey’s dogs and Toby for August 2023, but never confirmed a date or place. They wanted a safe trail where the dogs could run freely. Andrew and his girlfriend enjoy finding cafés and restaurants; on the weekend of April 8–9 they tried a café with croissants, muffins, and tarts. They picnicked July 7. Andrew volunteered with his girlfriend at an animal shelter July 24; Audrey had never volunteered but hoped to someday. Andrew planned camping with his girlfriend and Toby (Aug 4), visited a farm for vegetables (Aug 16), and went fishing with her Aug 19–20. He took a rock-climbing class June 11, reached the top with friends’ support, and liked the view; afterward he considered kayaking and possibly bungee jumping. He hikes with friends, including May 6–7 and June 23, and planned a nature-reserve visit Aug 19–20. Hiking calms and invigorates him; reaching a summit makes worries vanish.

Audrey bakes blueberry muffins and suggested a pastry party with Andrew in April; it remained a future plan with no date or location. She loves cooking as creative self-care, often with music and wine. Favorite: family chicken pot pie, which reminds her of her grandmother. She also loves garlic and Mediterranean-inspired roasted chicken with lemon and herbs. She offered recipes; Andrew said he would try them July 3. Andrew is a beginner cook who experiments to de-stress. By July 3 work and housing difficulties had led him to cook more and seek hobbies. Work stress curtailed outdoor time in July and September. On Sept 6 he said morning coffee and lunchtime walks helped him recharge; Audrey aims for one self-care activity daily. Audrey’s neighbors’ dogs had a playdate with hers by Sept 6. Andrew hiked over the Sept 2–3 weekend and photographed a sunset over the city. Earlier shared photos included dogs, trails, a mountain sunset with a church, horses, and Audrey’s dogs playing.

**Session 19 — September 24, 2023:** Andrew and Audrey resumed chatting after a long gap. Audrey said that the previous Friday, September 22, one of her dogs saw something at the park and pulled so hard that the leash broke. She feared the dog might run off or get hurt, chased and caught her safely, then calmed her with petting, hugs, a calm voice, and a slow walk. She said incidents like this remind her how important the dogs are and strengthen their bond. She shared a photo of a red retractable leash with black handle. Andrew sympathized and said he felt anxious imagining Toby getting lost; he referred to the dog as Precious, but Audrey had not specified which dog it was. He asked how to build a strong bond with Toby. Audrey advised patience, regular training, giving dogs time and love, and praising success. Andrew agreed dogs may need different amounts of time to bond.

They discussed Audrey’s dogs’ training, walks, breeds, and affection for them. Audrey said she walks them multiple times daily for exercise and bonding; all are mutts—two Jack Russell mixes and two Chihuahua mixes. Andrew shared a photo of flowers on his balcony and said caring for them was something he had been doing lately. Audrey said she has a small garden, with flowers and a growing vegetable patch, and finds watching plants grow relaxing, peaceful, and satisfying. Andrew asked about the flowers; Audrey identified them as Peruvian lilies, describing their bright colors and delicate petals. They are easy to care for, needing watering and enough sun. Audrey said the dogs enjoy running around and exploring the garden. The conversation ended with both emphasizing how much their dogs mean to them.
mem.28:
Andrew and Audrey — memory through November 22, 2023

Audrey and her dogs
- Adopted Pepper, Precious, Panda, and Pixie on April 2, 2023. They were about three years old by May. Breed descriptions varied: initially two Jack Russell mixes and two Chihuahua mixes; October 28 she said Pepper and Panda are Lab mixes, Precious and Pixie Chihuahua mixes. All are mutts.
- Pixie took a few days to settle in and bonded especially with Pepper. Audrey describes the dogs as cuddly, playful, mischievous, wise, and adventurous; usual resting spots: Pepper couch, Pixie bed, Precious chair, Panda rug. They mean everything to her.
- Walks them several times daily, often about an hour at their pace; they like sniffing, nature, running, and meeting dogs, but dislike snow. She plays fetch/frisbee, arranges playdates, visits parks, trails, beaches, and a national park. Leashes and safety matter to her. In June she had a yard with agility gear; by August took agility classes twice weekly. Uses positive reinforcement; teaches sit, stay, shake, roll over. Learned patient grooming: brushing, baths, ears/paws, nails.
- Knee injury once interrupted walks; later resumed. Joint vet visit in August was chaotic, so planned individual visits. A leash broke at a park September 22; she caught and soothed the dog. Dogs swam at a beach around September 30–October 1.
- In week of October 16 she injured/broke her arm playing with the dogs; cast made one-handed care hard, but she was improving October 24. Dogs acted unusually; she took them to a behaviorist October 25. Visit began hectic; behaviorist examined them, asked questions, advised routine/handling changes. Audrey used positive reinforcement and saw early progress; exact issues unspecified.
- Took all four to a pet salon Friday, November 17; they were excited, then calmed down and behaved well. On November 22 shared a groomed-dog photo (photo depicts one dog standing on a table with leash) and said their coats were shiny; she worries about them in new places and was happy they settled.
- Childhood dog Max loved fetch; Audrey remembers walks and confiding in him. Has dog/sunflower and four-dog arm tattoos, makes personalized wooden tags, and makes/sells recycled-material jewelry, donating some proceeds to an animal shelter. Would like to volunteer again but currently cannot.
- Gardens Peruvian lilies and vegetables; recycles and usually takes public transport. Cooking with music and wine is self-care. Favorite food is grandmother’s chicken pot pie, offered to Andrew; likes garlic and Mediterranean roast chicken with lemon/herbs. Dogs, cooking, and nature bring joy and peace.

Andrew
- Became a Financial Analyst during week of March 20, 2023. Loves animals/eagles and birdwatching; nature is restorative and spiritually grounding. Favorite trail Fox Hollow; tries to hike weekly. Work/city keep him indoors; enjoys greenery, mountains, fresh air, and sharing photos.
- In spring 2023 struggled to find dog-friendly housing and a small-apartment-suitable dog near parks/woods; Audrey offered housing-filter suggestions and help. Cooks to de-stress, considers himself a beginner. He and girlfriend enjoy cafés/pastries, picnics, farms, board games, and outdoors.
- Rock-climbed with friends June 11, reached top; considered kayaking/bungee jumping. Volunteered at shelter with girlfriend July 24; fished with her August 19–20. Work stress limited outdoor time; in September added morning coffee and lunch walks. Cares for balcony flowers.
- Got male German Shepherd Toby by July 11; smart, loyal, energetic, likes cute sweaters, once chased a squirrel around a tree. Later adopted male shelter dog Buddy; by October 19 Buddy was adjusting to home and Toby, who needed time to accept him. Walks Buddy, who likes trails.
- November 22 said he and girlfriend had adopted another dog “the other day,” named Scout after considering options; photo showed a woman feeding a dog hay in a barn. Plans to take Scout, Toby, and Buddy to a small nearby park. Keeping Scout leashed outdoors, bought bed, toys, and puppy pads, and was advised to introduce Scout to Toby and Buddy gradually. This conflicts with November 4, when Andrew had agreed to wait before adding another dog; Audrey had advised focusing on Toby and Buddy’s health and happiness.
- He and girlfriend went wine tasting October 21–22, enjoyed unusual wines and learned a lot. Recently tried sushi and liked it; Audrey suggested California/salmon rolls, sauces, new flavors. He promised photos; she admired his sushi photo and said she’d order sushi that night.

Shared plans/events/photos
- Repeatedly discussed dog-friendly hikes: hoped for August (no date/location), then November. Audrey offered to research; Andrew seek a safe rural trail. He invited Audrey and dogs July 11. Audrey invited him to a tree-lined park trail in June; he accepted.
- October 1 Andrew offered birdwatching; Audrey accepted pending schedules and planned to learn local birds. Andrew would bring binoculars/notebook; both find nature calming. He also offered riverside bike routes; she was interested. Audrey has nearby dog park with trees/benches. She likes lakes and recalled a peaceful mountain-lake trip; never fished. Andrew and girlfriend camped with Toby (planned August 4) and visited a vegetable farm. They discussed November beach trip with Toby on October 1.
- Photos over time: Audrey’s dogs in fields/woods, with ball/frisbee, at lake, after grooming; Andrew’s hiking, dogs, pastries, nature. Andrew hiked with friends May 6–7, June 23, and saw sunset hiking September 2–3. Audrey saw hummingbird hiking late April, shared two horses June 2, once drove three hours for scenic sunset. Andrew and girlfriend tried a pastry café April 8–9; Audrey suggested a pastry party, never scheduled. October 13 he proposed café with view or nearby park if dogs weren’t allowed.
- October 28: Andrew shared national-park mountain, dog-friendly trail, autumn forest, and himself hiking with happy dog photos. They agreed to plan a Saturday hike (date/time/trail unspecified), with snacks; he had Sunday picnic date with girlfriend. Discussed nearby peaceful lake trail and hoped to visit autumn forest trail for fall colors and dog photos. Both said friendship and outdoor time together mattered.
- November 4: Andrew and girlfriend had a good weekend bike ride and found park outside town; shared photo of two people biking on paved path. Audrey said dogs had run and gotten fresh air the previous weekend. She joined a dog owners’ group that meets weekly for tips and dog play; shared group-and-dogs-in-park photos. Andrew considered joining and getting another dog; Audrey advised focusing on Toby and Buddy, saying they didn’t need more dogs to be happy. Audrey shared dogs playing frisbee, a basket of stuffed toys, and a dog with tennis ball. City dog ownership, exercise, socialization, and mental stimulation discussed; Audrey uses puzzles, training, hide-and-seek, frisbee. Andrew planned to try enrichment ideas. They value mutual support and friendship.
- November 22: Audrey asked whether Andrew’s dogs had been groomed; he said not yet. They exchanged congratulations and encouragement about Scout and Audrey’s four dogs. She stressed leash safety, gradual exposure, and slow introductions. They both said dogs bring joy, friendship, and are family.
